inspection_summary: Inspected all 717 normalized lines. The source develops the zero-to-prime-power explicit density, tests its conditionally convergent truncations, uses Gaussian convolution to turn nonuniform lines into comparable responses, derives an exponentially damped sum rule and a resolution/error relation, and then separates genuine prime/zero structure from an invalid dynamical trace-formula analogy. Plot interiors and several displayed formulas have text-layer damage, but the selected mathematics is recoverable from checked prose and captions.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the numerical explicit-formula, line-intensity, Gaussian-sum-rule, convergence, and quantum-chaos agenda.

sections_inspected.label: I. Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Sets up the two directions between zeros and prime powers, the correlation contrast, the trace-formula question, and the finite-truncation resolution problem.

sections_inspected.label: II. Riemann's Formula
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives the prime-power counting and density representations from the Euler product and relates them to prime counting by Möbius inversion.

sections_inspected.label: III. Numerics: ordering
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Fixes increasing-zero order as essential for conditional convergence.

sections_inspected.label: III.A. Line Intensities of the Truncated Series
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Diagnoses nonuniform raw line shapes and constructs Gaussian convolution as an intensity-preserving, uniform-response extraction method with a resolution constraint.

sections_inspected.label: III.B. Sum Rule and Numerical Convergence
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives the Gaussian-damped absolutely convergent sum rule and converts its damping threshold into a maximum-resolvable-x and truncation-error rule.

sections_inspected.label: IV. Discussion and Conclusion
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Interprets phase, frequency, amplitude, scaling, off-critical perturbations, statistical contrast, and the obstruction to treating the formula as a dynamical trace formula.

sections_inspected.label: Acknowledgments, references, and technical notes
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Mostly nonmathematical back matter, with bounded caveats on convolution limits, a small-x inflection bound, and the trivial-zero smooth term.

accepted_units.title: Prime logarithms as periodic-orbit data for the zero spectrum
accepted_units.why_material: The text maps the oscillatory density of zeta zeros to a Gutzwiller-like orbit sum whose actions are logarithms of prime powers, making a precise structural analogy between arithmetic and spectral representations.
accepted_units.context_note: Self-contained introductory direction from primes to zeros; it explicitly marks the Hamiltonian as unknown.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the trace-formula vocabulary of density of states, actions, and periodic orbits, but the correspondence is stated in recoverable prose.

accepted_units.title: Correlated zeros interfere to locate nearly uncorrelated prime powers
accepted_units.why_material: The reverse direction is conceptually nontrivial: an infinite oscillatory series indexed by highly correlated zeros reconstructs the locally irregular prime-power sequence.
accepted_units.context_note: Contrasts the GUE-like zero sequence with Poisson-like prime spacings without claiming their statistics are identical.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses density decomposition into smooth and oscillatory parts; no unreadable display is required.

accepted_units.title: Why the inverse oscillatory formula need not be a dynamical trace formula
accepted_units.why_material: It distinguishes formal oscillatory resemblance from dynamical origin and explains what a separate trace formula for primes would and would not imply.
accepted_units.context_note: This is an early conceptual warning later justified by structural obstructions at lines 610-625.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends only on the stated contrast between oscillatory sums and periodic-orbit dynamics.

accepted_units.title: Truncation turns exact spikes into lines with unknown shape and resolution
accepted_units.why_material: It identifies the central finite-information problem: conditional convergence to delta spikes does not guarantee that a truncated sum has correct widths, shapes, or relative intensities, motivating both numerical and analytic controls.
accepted_units.context_note: Defines the paper's operative questions rather than asserting that truncation already solves them.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires distinguishing the infinite distributional density from a finite oscillatory approximation.

accepted_units.title: Euler product to the oscillatory prime-power density
accepted_units.why_material: The Euler product is logarithmically expanded, inverse-Laplace transformed into a weighted prime-power count, differentiated, and rewritten under RH as a smooth density plus cosine terms indexed by zeros; the text identifies interference of those terms as the source of prime-power spikes.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 unit carried at its exact span; its derivational setup and interpretation are locally present.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several displays have imperfect text extraction, but equations (1)-(3), the weights, the critical-line assumption, and the cosine-sum interpretation are recoverable from display fragments plus prose.

accepted_units.title: Weighted prime-power counts versus prime-only counts
accepted_units.why_material: The step function assigns reciprocal-power weights and Möbius inversion recovers the prime-counting function, clarifying why the density of all prime powers retains more direct information than a prime-only density.
accepted_units.context_note: Also records the historical finite-zero computation and why the authors choose the direct density formula.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the readable step-weight description and Möbius-inversion display; the historical Gram-series detail is supporting context.

accepted_units.title: Conditional convergence selects increasing-zero order
accepted_units.why_material: The finite computation is not permutation invariant: summing zeros in increasing imaginary part is the required natural order, while other selection rules can drive incorrect finite values.
accepted_units.context_note: The authors report numerical checks of this ordering sensitivity but do not supply a separate proof here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: No formula reconstruction is needed; the convergence constraint is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Gaussian convolution makes line heights comparable while exposing a resolution limit
accepted_units.why_material: Convolving the truncated density with an unnormalized Gaussian replaces sufficiently narrow peaks by nearly uniform Gaussian responses whose heights encode pre-convolution areas, avoiding oscillatory-tail integration errors and yielding an explicit width-versus-spacing resolution criterion.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 unit carried at its exact span; its opening inference and references to the raw signal require the bounded preceding line-shape evidence identified in v1_context_repairs.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (5)-(6) are readable; interpretation depends on delta-response intuition, the unnormalized unit-height Gaussian, and the condition that intrinsic linewidth be small relative to sigma.

accepted_units.title: Convolved line heights recover reciprocal prime-power multiplicities
accepted_units.why_material: The checked caption states that prime powers p^n appear at height 1/n after convolution, directly validating the relative-intensity semantics rather than mere peak location.
accepted_units.context_note: The plot interior is not selected; the caption supplies the recoverable result and parameters.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the Gaussian-convolution construction and on accepting the figure caption as reported numerical evidence.

accepted_units.title: Gaussian smoothing converts the conditional explicit formula into a damped sum rule
accepted_units.why_material: The source reframes convergence control as reproduction of a coarse-grained density, convolves each oscillatory term, locally freezes the slow amplitude and linearizes phase, and obtains an exponential damping factor in zero height.
accepted_units.context_note: The conceptual derivation is readable despite damaged intermediate display layout; the leading-order nature of the amplitude and phase approximations is explicit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-sensitive: relies on S_alpha(x)=alpha log x, a slowly varying amplitude, narrow Gaussian support, first-order phase expansion, and the Gaussian integral; scan verification would be prudent before exact symbolic reuse.

accepted_units.title: Exponential damping translates a zero cutoff into a controlled x range
accepted_units.why_material: Absolute convergence of the smoothed rule permits a threshold epsilon that relates alpha_max, sigma, and x_max; omitted terms are largest near the boundary and exponentially smaller below it, making resolution and truncation error tunable.
accepted_units.context_note: The numerical examples are presented as checks of the threshold relation, not a universal precision theorem; epsilon is chosen operationally.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equation (10) is formula-dependent but readable. Exact constants and the inflection-point restriction should be scan-checked before computational reuse.

accepted_units.title: The phase of zeta links zero locations and prime density
accepted_units.why_material: The phase jumps at zeros, its derivative contributes the oscillatory zero density, and a contour integral of log zeta yields the prime-power density, locating the bridge in a shared representation rather than in statistical similarity.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a conceptual synthesis stated by the authors; it does not construct the unknown Hamiltonian.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses phase and logarithmic-derivative language; the prose is recoverable without the cited derivation.

accepted_units.title: Resolution at large x requires increasingly high zeros
accepted_units.why_material: Logarithmic phase makes fixed terms oscillate more slowly and decay as x grows, so constructive interference at larger prime powers requires higher-frequency zeros; conditional convergence prevents replacing the natural initial segment by high zeros alone, leading to impractical scaling.
accepted_units.context_note: The unit's prose is interrupted by the page-12 Figure 5 plot at lines 548-583; the sentence resumes at line 585 and remains recoverable, while the caption independently confirms the predicted boundary.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the phase alpha log x, the natural-order constraint, and equation (10); the embedded plot interior is extraction-defective and is not used for exact values beyond its caption.

accepted_units.title: Moving zeros off the critical line separates peak location from intensity
accepted_units.why_material: The source changes the real parts of zeros while retaining imaginary parts and reports that prime-power peak locations persist but relative intensities fail, distinguishing frequency/phase control from amplitude control.
accepted_units.context_note: This is reported numerical evidence and does not establish RH; the generalized off-line factor is attributed to a reference.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-sensitive: the replacement amplitude x^(1-gamma) is legible in prose/display, but exact generalized-formula use would require the cited source or scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Missing repetitions and orbit-dependent amplitudes block a dynamical trace-formula reading
accepted_units.why_material: The proposed orbit identification fails because there are no repetition indices, the implied trajectories are not periodic, amplitudes lack zero-index dependence, and a single Hamiltonian is unlikely to reproduce both oscillatory and smooth energy dependence.
accepted_units.context_note: This supplies the detailed justification for the earlier analogy limit at lines 65-79.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses semiclassical trace-formula expectations as comparison criteria; footnote 17 separately corrects which smooth term could count as Thomas-Fermi.

accepted_units.title: Small-x behavior refines the inflection-point upper bound
accepted_units.why_material: The technical note records a more accurate small-x inflection bound and warns that including the logarithmic amplitude changes the inflection condition to a transcendental equation.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a bounded refinement of the convergence criterion, not a replacement for equation (10).
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The radical expression is text-layer fragile and requires scan verification before exact reuse; the qualitative refinement is recoverable from prose.

accepted_units.title: The trivial-zero smooth term is not Thomas-Fermi data
accepted_units.why_material: This corrects the dynamical analogy by excluding the second smooth term of equation (3), which arises from trivial zeros, from the proposed Thomas-Fermi contribution.
accepted_units.context_note: A concise footnote tied directly to the trace-formula interpretation at lines 610-625.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on equation (3)'s decomposition and semiclassical Thomas-Fermi terminology; no damaged formula is needed.

v1_context_repairs.reason: The immutable unit begins 'Thus' and refers to the original signal and Figure 1; lines 184-270 supply the subsection framing and checked evidence that truncated raw lines have nonuniform shapes, which is the exact motivation for Gaussian convolution and meaningful intensity comparison.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From conditional explicit formula to controlled coarse-grained reconstruction
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The source turns an ordering-sensitive distributional identity into a usable finite diagnostic by smoothing peaks into a common response, which exponentially damps high-zero contributions and makes the reliable x-range and boundary error explicit.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The Gaussian sum rule uses local amplitude and first-order phase approximations, and the resulting control is for the smoothed density under the chosen sigma and epsilon, not direct unconditional control of the original spike series.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The same zero data support an arithmetic bridge but not the proposed dynamics
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Shared phase/oscillation structure gives meaningful two-way prime/zero representations, while missing orbit repetitions, index-independent amplitudes, and the trivial-zero smooth term prevent upgrading that resemblance to a Hamiltonian trace formula.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The obstruction applies to Riemann's formula as written and does not rule out a different trace formula or Hamiltonian for the prime spectrum.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Frequency fixes locations while amplitude fixes weights
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The reported off-critical perturbation, read beside the reciprocal-power intensity check, suggests that imaginary parts control the interference locations whereas real parts control the reconstructed weights.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is solver- and experiment-conditional evidence reported by the paper, not a proof that arbitrary zero perturbations preserve every peak or that RH follows from correct intensities.

within_source_saturation: Saturated for source-grounded semantic segmentation: every recoverable mathematical mechanism, comparison, obstruction, counterfactual, convergence condition, and bounded technical caveat is either selected or represented as support. Further units would predominantly duplicate the introduction/conclusion, isolate routine numerical examples, or promote plot/text-layer defects and bibliography.
